card.title: Equilibrium Constant Expression and Its Importance

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Kc is a number that speaks. **Big Kc** (10⁵ and up) declares the reaction practically complete; **small Kc** (10⁻⁵ and down) declares it stillborn; **Kc near 1** declares a true contest. The same fraction evaluated off-equilibrium is the **reaction quotient Qc** — Qc < Kc drives forward, Qc > Kc drives back, Qc = Kc is the resting state — making the constant a compass as well as a scoreboard.…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: - Kc = [C]^c[D]^d / [A]^a[B]^b - Qc = same expression, non-equilibrium concentrations - ΔG° = −RT ln K - N₂ + 3H₂ ⇌ 2NH₃: Kc = [NH₃]²/([N₂][H₂]³); NEB 2024: [NH₃] = 0.25 M

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: ❌ All atoms are identical in an element. ✅ Isotopes have same protons but different neutrons.  ·  ❌ Atoms are indivisible. ✅ Atoms consist of protons, neutrons, and electrons.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: ***The 0.25 M answer*** — the exact numerical NEB 2024 demanded: square the hydrogen concentration (0.125), multiply by Kc (0.0625), take the root (0.25 M). Four lines, full marks.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: ❌ Electrons orbit in fixed paths like planets. ✅ Electrons exist in probability clouds (orbitals).  ·  ❌ Heisenberg uncertainty means we cannot measure position and momentum precisely simultaneously — not that we lack good instruments.

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Numerical recipe: expression → substitute → isolate square → root. (0.5)³ = 0.125 by heart. Qc<Kc → forward. Big Kc = product-rich.

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: The single most reused NEB skill: substitute equilibrium concentrations into the mass-action fraction and solve for the unknown — every power is an exponent, every solid is silent.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Kc ≫ 1: products dominate; Kc ≪ 1: reactants dominate; Kc ≈ 1: both appreciable. Qc (same expression, any moment): Qc<Kc forward, Qc>Kc reverse, Qc=Kc equilibrium. Kc depends only on T. Importance: extent, direction, ΔG° = −RT ln K, industrial design. Worked NEB 2024: Kc = 0.5 = [NH3]2/(1.0 × 0.125) → [NH3] = 0.25 M.

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Atmospheric nitrogen and oxygen coexist because Kc for NO formation is ~10⁻³¹ at 25 °C — the same reaction runs furiously inside engines at 2500 K, where Kc leaps and smog is born.

rows.label: More practice
rows.text: **NEB-style (2m): For N₂O₄(g) ⇌ 2NO₂(g), Kc = 4.0 at temperature T. A vessel contains [N₂O₄] = 0.5 M and [NO₂] = 1.0 M. Predict the direction of the net reaction.** — Compute the reaction quotient with the same expression as Kc: Qc = [NO₂]²/[N₂O₄] = (1.0)²/(0.5) = 2.0.…

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: ## 1. Topic Introduction — Reading the Constant, Computing the Concentration Kc is more than a fraction: its **size** grades how far a reaction proceeds, its **units** encode the stoichiometry, and its algebra solves the classic NEB numerical — "given some equilibrium concentrations, find the missing one." This topic turns the law of mass action into a working calculator.  ·  ## 2. Fundamental Concepts ### 2.1 What the size of Kc means - **Kc very large (≫1):** products dominate at equilibrium — reaction nearly complete (e.g. Kc ~ 10²⁵ for H₂ + ½O₂ → H₂O at 25 °C). - **Kc very small (≪1):** reactants dominate — hardly any conversion (e.g. N₂ + O₂ ⇌ 2NO, Kc ~ 10⁻³¹ at 25 °C). - **Kc ≈ 1:** appreciable amounts of both — a genuine balance.…  ·  ## 3. Scientific Definitions | Term | Scientific meaning | Example | |---|---|---| | **Equilibrium constant Kc** | Ratio of product to reactant active masses at equilibrium, fixed T | [NH₃]²/([N₂][H₂]³) | | **Reaction quotient Qc** | Same ratio with arbitrary concentrations | Direction indicator | | **Extent of reaction** | Degree of conversion at equilibrium, graded by Kc…

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: ❌ de Broglie wavelength applies only to light. ✅ All matter has wave nature; detectable mainly for small masses like electrons.  ·  ❌ Quantum number l can be any integer. ✅ l ranges from 0 to n−1.  ·  ❌ Magnetic quantum number ml determines energy. ✅ ml determines orbital orientation, not energy (in absence of magnetic field).

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: ❌ Spin quantum number ms can be ±½ or any value. ✅ ms is always +½ or −½.  ·  ❌ Aufbau principle means filling from bottom to top of the diagram. ✅ Fill lowest-energy orbitals first: 1s→2s→2p→3s→3p→4s→3d→4p→...  ·  ❌ Pauli exclusion allows two electrons per orbital with any spin. ✅ Two electrons in same orbital must have opposite spins.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: ❌ Hund's rule means pair electrons before spreading. ✅ Electrons fill degenerate orbitals singly first with parallel spins.  ·  ❌ The mole is just a number like dozen. ✅ 1 mole = 6.022×10²³ particles (Avogadro constant) — a bridge between atomic and macroscopic scales.  ·  ❌ Molar mass and molecular mass are the same thing. ✅ Molecular mass is in amu; molar mass is in g/mol — numerically equal but different units.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: ❌ Limiting reagent is the reactant with smallest mass. ✅ Limiting reagent is the one that produces the least product (determined by moles, not mass).  ·  ❌ % yield can exceed 100%. ✅ % yield >100% indicates impure product or incomplete drying.  ·  ❌ Molarity and molality are the same. ✅ Molarity = mol/L solution (changes with T); Molality = mol/kg solvent (temperature-independent).

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: ❌ A strong acid completely ionizes in water. ✅ Strong acids (HCl, HNO₃, H₂SO₄) are ~100% ionized; weak acids partially ionize.  ·  ❌ pH can be negative. ✅ pH < 0 is possible for concentrations >1M (e.g., 2M HCl has pH ≈ −0.3).  ·  ❌ Kc changes when concentration changes. ✅ Kc is constant at constant temperature; only temperature changes K.
